pairs.difference: A: the cap board is one quiet, soft matte surface with a rounded edge and only a soft sheen on the button, like the lesson REAL cards. B: the boot shaft has a fine mottled leather grain, crisp inlay edges, a sharp raised overlay and a hard polished rivet and spur, so it carries more micro-finish than real cards do.
pairs.fix: Paint the boot leather as one smooth, soft satin surface with no pore grain; soften the inlay edges and keep the rivet a simple soft dot.

pairs.difference: A: the star's silver facets have a pearly, speckled sheen with fine noise, and the gold rim and balls are evenly lacquered, so the whole badge is one coated finish. B: the wristband is soft matte rubber with a smooth gradient and slightly raised, softly shaded icons, with no surface noise.
pairs.fix: Make the star's silver plate clean smooth metal with one broad soft highlight and no speckle; keep the gold rim less shiny than the ball tips.

pairs.difference: A: the jacket has many crisp parts, including sharply edged badges, pocket flaps and sash piping, on a clay-like cloth; detail and micro-texture sit just above the real range. B: the hat is soft, quiet felt with a faint even mottle and only one crisp spot, the buckle. The call is weak because both are mostly matte.
pairs.fix: Soften the badge rims and flap edges and make the sash the same quiet soft cloth as the jacket, with fewer sharp small details.

pairs.difference: A: the ticket is plain and flat with soft edges, no material marks and a slightly uneven dotted line; it is odd but has no invented texture. B: the sign planks have large decorative cracks, split ends, knot swirls and heavy carved grain lines, with hard round bolts, so the grain is big and ornamental rather than the fine quiet grain of the real podium and swing.
pairs.fix: Draw the planks as smooth painted wood with only a few faint thin grain lines; remove the big cracks, knot swirls and split ends.

pairs.difference: A: the cactus is clean waxy green with soft ribs and small simple spines; the pot is matte clay. B: the vending machine glass is covered in speckled condensation dots that smear over cans whose labels have melted, and the blue body is glossy, so it reads as noise and AI smear rather than deliberate detail.
pairs.fix: Show clear, clean glass with one soft diagonal reflection and no droplets; give the cans simple crisp labels.

pairs.difference: A: the beach ball is smooth vinyl with very soft blended highlights and no small detail, and its measurements are low only because the subject is plain. B: the saddle has fine dashed stitching along every edge, leather pore grain, punched strap holes and crisp buckle metal, the same added dashed-stitch finish seen on the lesson generated gloves.
pairs.fix: Remove the dashed stitch lines and pore grain; paint the saddle as smooth soft leather with a few simple raised seams and a broad soft highlight.

pairs.difference: A: the rope has crisp, uniform twist lines from end to end, and the beam has fine sharp streaked grain; gloss share 0.42 is far above the real maximum of 0.267. B: the sneakers are busy with mesh dots and candy laces, but the rubber, mesh and collar finishes differ and they sit at the top edge of the real range. Both look over-detailed, so the call is weak.
pairs.fix: Make the rope a soft, chunky twist with fewer, blended strand lines and a matte finish; quiet the beam grain to a few faint lines.

pairs.difference: A: the fountain stone is soft and clay-smooth with quiet shading and simple scallops; the paving is plain. B: the wagon canvas has a visible fine weave and creased hem, the planks have sharp grain lines and nail heads, and the ground is speckled; highlight share 0.206 is above the real range. It has more crisp micro-texture than real cards do.
pairs.fix: Paint the canvas as smooth soft cloth with no weave and only large gentle folds; keep the planks plain with a few faint grain lines and no nail heads.

pairs.difference: A: the enamel pot has chipped paint flakes, rust nicks, thin scratches and a dent on a satin surface, so the wear reads as realistic weathering that real cards here do not use. B: the tray is clean soft plastic with glossy ice cubes; its frost specks are noisy but only appear at the edges. Measurements give no separation.
pairs.fix: Remove the scratches, rust nicks and chipped flakes; paint the pot as clean soft blue enamel with a broad gentle highlight.

pairs.difference: A: the saloon has dense, crisp, evenly repeated plank lines, roof ribs and sharp window frames across the whole building, and gloss sits right at the real maximum. B: the pier is softer, with chunky blended rope, simple plank shading and a smooth life ring; the post has some cracks but the overall finish stays quiet.
pairs.fix: Reduce the plank lines to wider, softer boards with faint grain and soften the window frame and roof rib edges so the surface reads quieter.

pairs.difference: A: the locomotive is lacquered all over, with sharp specular streaks on the black boiler, polished gold bands and crisp rivets; detail 0.0789 and gloss 0.294 are both above the real range. B: the bus has soft satin red paint, blurred window reflections and simple forms, in range and close to the real taxi and plane.
pairs.fix: Give the boiler a soft satin black with one broad dim highlight, make the gold bands less polished, and use fewer, softer rivets.

pairs.difference: A: this is a re-render of the anchor Ferris wheel. The spokes are pale, featureless plastic with no wood tone or grain, and the rear struts melt into smeared crossings, which is AI smear in the structure. B: the jellyfish has a wet glossy gradient with clean translucent frills and bubbles and no smear.
pairs.fix: Paint the spokes as light wood with faint fine grain and clean separate rear struts; no merged or smeared beams.

pattern: Generated cards are given away by surface finish that is added everywhere at one sharpness: dashed stitching, leather pore grain, canvas weave, decorative cracks and knots, repeated plank lines, scratches and speckle. They also lean toward an even lacquer, or a speckled sheen on metal and glass. Some have smeared small structures, such as melted struts or droplet noise. Real cards stay quieter, with soft blended materials, few marks, one broad highlight and crispness saved for a few focal spots.
